findings.what: Both newly added player units declare SetupElevator as void, while its new accepted definition returns char and its elevator caller uses that byte result. This is an avoidable cross-unit return-type mismatch, not required by the original bytes. Changing only those declarations to char preserves every function in both whole files for both revisions. The new scene also chooses int abs while the new transition unit uses long; the scene long alternative independently matches. These do not produce a binary discrepancy, but do not satisfy a claim of consistent extern types.
findings.suggested_fix: Move SetupElevator out of the void declaration lists and use extern char SetupElevator() in both player files. Private alternatives/char-SetupElevator/ contains both complete matching files. Prefer the long abs declaration already used by the adjacent transition unit/runtime consumers; alternatives/long-abs/elevator_scene.c matches both revisions. Do not claim the older repository-wide abs disagreement is thereby fully reconciled.

findings.what: The new scene declares the named TOEJAM_FALL_STATE object as a scalar char and assigns it directly, while the existing and newly added player/graphics units declare the same named object as char[]. This differs from using the separate named ram_ffda23 byte and is an avoidable incompatible extern view. The array declaration and [0] store preserve all 21 scene functions byte-for-byte in both revisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Use extern char TOEJAM_FALL_STATE[] and TOEJAM_FALL_STATE[0] = 0. The complete alternative is alternatives/array-fall-state/elevator_scene.c; the combined alternatives/consistent-scene-interfaces/elevator_scene.c also matches both revisions.

findings.what: func_012762 is described as setting an elevator position and accepts struct elevator_record *, but its only catalogued direct caller, func_010968 at 0x010a94, passes a player object. The helper only writes x/y at offsets 0/2, so the incorrect record view happens to reproduce the bytes. The concrete pointer type and comment mislead readers about the caller and object being updated.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare its parameter as struct elevator_entity *player, use player->x/y, and describe the saved map-cell coordinates being applied to the player. alternatives/player-coordinate-helper/elevator_scene.c makes only this correction and MATCHes the complete 21-function scene in both revisions; the combined interface alternative also matches. No speculative original bug annotation or address cast is needed.

findings.what: The signed-long casts on the shared unsigned flags_52 field exist solely to obtain the observed scratch-register allocation. The author handoff discloses that fact, but neither source file does. Cast-free natural alternatives fail, while making the field long and removing the casts matches both complete units; that does not prove historical signedness and would introduce a different shared-type conflict if adopted only here. The existing legal scalar casts are not prohibited pointer tricks or behavioral bugs, but their reason should not be hidden.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief local compiler-choice qualification at these tests: the signed 32-bit value view preserves the observed D0 mask/allocation while the common storage remains unsigned; exact historical spelling/signedness is [INFERENCE]. Keep the shared field type unchanged unless an explicit whole-project interface reconciliation is performed. Alternative outcomes and listings are retained under alternatives/ and matches/alternatives-*/.

qualification_summary: No blocking byte mismatch, prohibited source device, stale prepare input or false-positive mutation control was found. The four C011 fixes are resolved. Acceptance remains qualified by the four low-severity source/interface/readability findings, plus explicitly recorded older interface/layout debt. All proposed alternatives are private experiments, not adopted sources; any source fixes require a newly prepared checkpoint. No independent suite rerun or gameplay execution is claimed.
